comments: Configuration for the VAMS v2.6 to v2.7 migration (asset location folder keys + asset location file to folder + orphaned workflow-trigger cleanup + bucket read constraints + vector index backfill + system-pipeline retirement report + comment and subscription keys + asset location index backfill). The single script v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py runs all steps; select one with --steps. commentSubscriptionKeys runs first, then assetLocationFolderKeys, first of the location steps, then assetLocationFileToFolder; assetLocationIndex runs last: the index is built from the fixed keys.
_comment_prefix: Required: SSM resource-name base prefix from the CDK core stack output 'ResourceNamesSSMParamPrefixOutput' (format: /{configName}-{baseStackName}-{region}/resourceNames). Every table and function name below is resolved from it; the explicit overrides are only needed when the prefix is not filled in.
_comment_location_tables: Both location steps, assetLocationFolderKeys and assetLocationIndex, read these two tables. Each is resolved from the prefix; set it only to override that name.
_comment_location_step: ===== STEP: assetLocationFolderKeys (runs first of the location steps, after commentSubscriptionKeys) =====
_comment_location: Scans every asset row (archived rows included). For a location key with no trailing '/', it reads the object at the key (HeadObject) and, when there is none, lists at most one key under '{key}/' (ListObjectsV2, MaxKeys=1) and, when that lists nothing, at most one version under '{key}/' (ListObjectVersions, MaxKeys=1, for an archived folder). A key with objects under it, current or archived, and none at it names a folder: a real run appends the '/', conditional on the key being unchanged, so a repeat changes nothing. A key with no objects at all, and a key that cannot be read, is reported only. Every finding is one line of assetLocationFolderKeys-<dry-run|execute>-report-<UTC time>.jsonl (one report per run; --resume appends to the report of the run it continues) in asset_location_output_dir (default: the working directory); the scan position is saved there after every page, and --resume continues from it. asset_location_pace_seconds is the pause after each key that needed an Amazon S3 read (default 0.05). CHANGES ASSET ROWS, so the account-id confirmation applies.
_comment_location_copy: Part (b): for a single-file location whose copy '{key}/{name}' exists, the copy's records move from '/{name}' to '/{name}/{name}' in the tables below (resolved from the prefix; the legacy V1 file versions table is skipped when not published). Each record is re-read (consistent read) and deleted only if unchanged since then; a record already at the new path is never overwritten (the clash is reported), and a record edited during the move stays, its asset unmarked, and the step exits non-zero so a re-run moves it. A copy of the copy ('{key}/{name}/{name}'), whether or not the copy is still there, is reported for a move by hand, and on a real run the step exits non-zero until its records are moved and its asset row is marked (see the README). While the step has not finished, a real run skips vectorBackfill and metadataBackfill. Vectors and execution history are not changed: run vectorBackfill afterwards. A real run marks each single-file asset row it finished (assetLocationCopyRecordsMovedAt) and every later run skips marked rows. File metadata and attributes carry no time, so run the step before users edit metadata on single-file assets.
_comment_file_to_folder: Converts every asset whose location key names a file (no trailing '/') into a folder asset. In place: the location becomes the file's parent folder when that folder holds only the asset's own keys and no other asset's location is on or in it; no Amazon S3 object is written, and the records and vector items of the companion entries whose path changes move from '/{path}' to '/{name}/{path}' (never over a record already there), then the changed files are re-indexed for search. A key with nothing stored at it gets its '/'. Every other layout is refused and reported, and the row is left unchanged. It reads the asset, bucket registration and path-keyed tables named above and writes the asset history and vector tables below. Report: assetLocationFileToFolder-<dry-run|execute>-report-<UTC time>.jsonl in asset_location_output_dir; --resume continues from its checkpoint. CHANGES ASSET ROWS, so the account-id confirmation applies.
_comment_file_to_folder_resolutions: Optional path to a JSON Lines file of per-asset choices for refused assets, one object per line: {"databaseId": ..., "assetId": ..., "fromKey": <the location as the report wrote it>, "resolution": "move" | "include-siblings"}. move copies the file (every version) and its previews into its companion folder '{key}/{name}' and puts a delete marker on the originals, so the file's S3 key changes; include-siblings lets the other files in the folder join the asset. Absent or null: no move and no include-siblings.
_comment_triggers: Deletes WorkflowTriggersStorageTable rows whose workflow is archived, missing, or one of the two retired built-ins (genai-metadata-3d-labeling-obj-glb-fbx-ply-stl-usd, metadata-extraction-cad-mesh under GLOBAL). Idempotent. DELETES ROWS, so the account-id confirmation applies.
_comment_bucket_read: From v2.7 GET /buckets lists a bucket, and POST /database and PUT /database/{databaseId} put a database on one, only for a role that may read it through a bucket constraint; a role stored before 2.7.0 holds those routes and no bucket constraint. This step reads the api and bucket constraints of the constraints table (Query on its ObjectTypeIndex) and the database ids (Scan of the database table, archived databases left out) and, for each role whose own constraints allow GET /buckets, POST /database or PUT /database/<id> for one of those databases (decided as the authorizer decides it) and that has no bucket constraint, writes the bucket constraint the shipped role templates carry: '<role>-buckets', GET on every registration (bucketId contains .*), one PutItem conditional on the item not existing, under an id derived from the role name. It changes no other constraint, leaves a role that already has any bucket constraint as it is, reports users granted a route directly without changing them, and leaves a role whose constraints cannot be read unchanged. One JSON line per role, naming the routes that qualified it, goes to bucketReadConstraints-<dry-run|execute>-report-<UTC time>.jsonl in bucket_read_constraints_output_dir (default: the working directory). A repeat writes nothing for a role that still has a bucket constraint, but gives the bucket read again to a role whose bucket constraint was removed after the first run: run it during the upgrade only. Skipping it: re-import the templates (or add a bucket constraint by hand) for the roles that list buckets or create or update databases. WRITES CONSTRAINTS, so the account-id confirmation applies. constraints_storage_table_name and database_storage_table_name are resolved from the prefix; set one only to override it.
_comment_vector: Invokes the deployed vectorReindexer Lambda (SSM key lambdaFunctions/vectorReindexer). clear_vectors=false re-embeds every latest live file in place (reindexer operation 'enqueue'); clear_vectors=true deletes every stored vector first (operation 'both'). A real run launches one Bedrock-billed execution per file either way, so the account-id confirmation applies. The step first reads the deployment's VECTORSEARCH feature switch (app feature table, resolved from the prefix): absent, vector search is off and the step is skipped with exit 0 (under --steps all and --steps vectorBackfill alike, whether or not a reindexer is published); present with no reindexer to invoke, or a state that cannot be read, is an error. vector_reindexer_function_name is used only while the switch is present. Upgrading with vector search on: run the migration. Off: nothing else is needed. Turning it on later (or off and on again): deploy with app.vectorSearch.enabled true, then run --steps vectorBackfill.
_comment_metadata: With vector search off and the SYSTEM GenAI metadata pipeline on, set this to true (or pass --generate-metadata-for-existing-files for one run) to analyze every existing latest live file: the step invokes the vectorReindexer with operation 'enqueue', and the system workflow writes the files' attributes and GenAI metadata (no vectors). One Bedrock-billed analysis run per file, so the account-id confirmation applies. Skipped when false, with vector search on (vectorBackfill analyzes every file), and when the pipeline is not enabled (no reindexer published); an unreadable or inconsistent state is an error. clear_vectors does not apply. Turning the pipeline on later with vector search off: deploy, then run --steps metadataBackfill with this set.
_comment_retirement: Lists executions of the retired workflows that are still in flight and user workflows that reference a retired pipeline id, with guidance. Writes nothing. workflow_storage_table_name_v2 above is reused.
_comment_comments_step: ===== STEP: commentSubscriptionKeys (required after the v2.7 deploy when the deployment has comments or subscriptions) =====
_comment_comments: Copies every row of the v2.6 comment and subscription tables (keyed by the asset id alone, published under dynamoTables/legacy/) into the v2.7 tables keyed by database and asset id. For each row it reads the asset table's assetIdGSI and the permanentDelete records of the asset history table (one filtered scan per run): a database whose asset with the id was permanently deleted counts as a candidate too, except for a comment made after that delete. The asset history table is the one asset_history_storage_table_name names in the assetLocationFileToFolder section above. One candidate places the row there (a subscriber only when it is on that asset's notification topic, else it is reported 'notOnTopic'); when several do, a comment goes to the one whose asset existed when the comment was made and, when any candidate has the comment's asset version, has that version (asset_versions_storage_table_name above), each subscriber of a subscription to the one whose notification topic carries that subscriber (SNS ListSubscriptionsByTopic, e-mails from the user table), so one v2.6 row can be split between databases, and otherwise (a comment, or a subscriber on no candidate's topic or on several) to the database comment_subscription_resolution_file names for the id (a JSON object {"<assetId>": "<databaseId>"}, honoured only for a database that holds the id). A comment or subscriber none of these places is reported 'ambiguous' and left where it is; one the evidence or the mapping gives to a permanently deleted asset is reported 'noAsset'. Run this step right after the deploy, before users permanently delete assets or change subscriptions (it runs first under --steps all). Soft-deleted comments are copied to the asset's '#deleted' partition. A V2 row is never overwritten: a subscriber is added with an update conditional on the list read, a comment or subscriber already there is 'alreadyPresent', and a comment id already used by another comment of the asset is reported 'duplicateCommentId'. Each comment and subscriber copied gets a copy record in the V2 comment table (partition '#commentSubscriptionKeys:<assetId>', sort key a SHA-256 hash of the v2.6 row key and subscriber, so no user id is stored in clear), written in the same transaction: a later run reports it 'alreadyCopied' and leaves it as users left it (edited, deleted, unsubscribed), so a re-run after adding a mapping entry copies only what earlier runs left. No v2.6 row is written or deleted. One JSON line per comment row and per subscriber goes to commentSubscriptionKeys-<dry-run|execute>-report.jsonl in comment_subscription_output_dir (default: the working directory), the scan position and report length are saved there after every page (--resume cuts the report back and continues, reporting each row once), and writes are paced to comment_subscription_writes_per_second. WRITES ROWS, so the account-id confirmation applies. These table names, and the asset and asset versions tables named at the top of this file, are resolved from the prefix; set one only to override it.
_comment_index_step: ===== STEP: assetLocationIndex (required once after the v2.7 deploy) =====
_comment_index: Writes locationBucket and locationKey on every asset row whose attributes are missing or differ from the row's location (one conditional UpdateItem per row, paced to asset_location_writes_per_second), verifies every row with strongly consistent scans, writes a report of the rows it could not index to asset_location_report_file, and writes the completion marker (SSM String parameter <prefix>/dataMigrations/assetLocationIndex) last. An interrupted run resumes from asset_location_checkpoint_file; a second run writes no row. A run stopped by limit never writes the marker. Makes no S3 call. It reads the asset and bucket registration tables named at the top of this file. Writes every asset row, so the account-id confirmation applies.
_comment_safety: ===== Shared safety options (apply to every step) =====
_comment_dry_run: Shipped true: while true, every run is a dry run even with --execute. Set it to false once the dry run's counts look right; a real run then still needs --execute on the command line.
_comment_aws: AWS configuration (optional - override with CLI flags)
_comment_instructions: How to use this configuration file
_instructions: === SETUP ===
1. Deploy the v2.7 CDK stack first. The deploy archives the retired built-ins, creates the vector
table and index, registers the system pipeline, and publishes the resource names to SSM.
2. Get the SSM resource-name base prefix from the CDK core stack outputs:
aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name your-vams-stack \
--query 'Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey==`ResourceNamesSSMParamPrefixOutput`].OutputValue' \
--output text
3. Set 'resource_names_ssm_param_prefix' in this file to that value, and set 'aws_region' (and
'aws_profile' if needed). Every table name and the vectorReindexer function name are then
resolved automatically from SSM Parameter Store.
=== EXECUTION (single consolidated script; --steps selects which step to run, default all) ===
4. Dry run first (the default - nothing is deleted or launched), all steps:
python v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py --config v2.6_to_v2.7_migration_config.json
5. Set dry_run to false in this file, then run for real. The script asks you to type the resolved
AWS account id, because orphanedTriggers deletes rows and vectorBackfill launches Bedrock-billed
executions (pass --confirm-account <account-id> instead of answering the prompt in automation):
python v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py --config v2.6_to_v2.7_migration_config.json --execute
6. Run only one step if needed:
python v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py --config v2.6_to_v2.7_migration_config.json --execute --steps orphanedTriggers
python v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py --config v2.6_to_v2.7_migration_config.json --execute --steps vectorBackfill
python v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py --config v2.6_to_v2.7_migration_config.json --steps systemPipelineRetirement
python v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py --config v2.6_to_v2.7_migration_config.json --execute --steps assetLocationIndex
python v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py --config v2.6_to_v2.7_migration_config.json --execute --steps commentSubscriptionKeys
7. (Vector rebuild only) Clear every stored vector before re-embedding:
python v2.6_to_v2.7_migration.py --config v2.6_to_v2.7_migration_config.json --execute --steps vectorBackfill --clear-vectors
=== WHAT THIS DOES ===
assetLocationFolderKeys: finds asset rows whose location key has no trailing '/', no object at the key
and objects under '{key}/', and appends the '/' on a real run; for a single-file asset whose copy
'{key}/{name}' exists it moves the copy's records from '/{name}' to '/{name}/{name}'. Runs first of the location steps. Report and checkpoint go to
asset_location_output_dir; --resume continues a stopped run.
assetLocationFileToFolder: converts each asset whose location names a file into a folder asset (in place
on the parent folder when it holds only the asset's keys, '/' appended when nothing is at the key, a move
or include-siblings only for the assets in asset_location_file_to_folder_resolutions). Runs after it; every
other layout is reported and left unchanged. Report and checkpoint go to asset_location_output_dir.
orphanedTriggers: enumerates every fileUpload trigger row through TriggersByBaseTypeGSI, joins it to
WorkflowStorageTableV2, and deletes rows whose workflow is archived or missing - including the two
retired built-ins' triggers, which otherwise keep firing into '400 Workflow is archived'.
bucketReadConstraints: gives each role whose constraints allow GET /buckets, POST /database or
PUT /database/{databaseId} and that has no bucket constraint the bucket read the shipped role templates
carry; changes no other constraint. Report goes to bucket_read_constraints_output_dir.
vectorBackfill: invokes the deployed vectorReindexer with {operation: enqueue|both, dryRun, limit}. The
reindexer enumerates the latest live version of every file and enqueues one system-workflow
execution per file (paced by app.vectorSearch.indexingConcurrency). The step returns when the work is
ENQUEUED; watch progress with: vamscli execution list --workflow-database-id GLOBAL
--workflow-id system-genai-metadata --trigger-type System-Reindex --status RUNNING
systemPipelineRetirement: reports in-flight executions of the retired workflows (they turn FAILED after
their task timeout) and user workflows still referencing a retired pipeline id. Read-only.
commentSubscriptionKeys: copies every v2.6 comment and subscription into the tables keyed by database and
asset id, placing an id several databases hold by evidence or by comment_subscription_resolution_file and
reporting the rest. Required once after the v2.7 deploy when comments or subscriptions exist; resumable;
a repeat copies only what earlier runs left and never undoes a user's change; never writes a v2.6 row.
assetLocationIndex: writes locationBucket and locationKey on every asset row, verifies them, writes a report
of the rows it could not index, then writes the completion marker the backend reads before any decision
uses the location index. Required once after the v2.7 deploy; resumable and safe to repeat.
=== SAFETY ===
- Every run is a dry run unless --execute is given AND dry_run above is false. Dry run: orphanedTriggers
names each row it would delete; vectorBackfill passes dryRun to the reindexer (it counts instead of
enqueueing); systemPipelineRetirement is unaffected (it only reads)
- A real run that deletes rows (orphanedTriggers), deletes vectors (--clear-vectors), or launches
Bedrock-billed executions (vectorBackfill, with or without --clear-vectors) is confirmed against the
resolved AWS account id: type it at the prompt or pass --confirm-account <account-id>. No flag skips
the check; an unresolved identity, or a non-interactive run without --confirm-account, is refused
- limit: caps trigger rows examined / files enqueued / rows listed per report section (testing only)
- clear_vectors: vectorBackfill only; defaults to false; natural-language search returns nothing between
the clear and the completion of the re-embedding executions
- Every step is safe to repeat: orphanedTriggers finds nothing on a second run, vectorBackfill overwrites
the same vector items and the system workflow's perInputFileVersion lock drops a duplicate launch,
systemPipelineRetirement writes nothing.
